initial.prompt:
Create a finished high resolution LANDSCAPE spacecraft CONCEPT REFERENCE SHEET, a calm professional industrial-design presentation for a retro-futurist PC exploration game, title "AURORA / 01". FOUR views of EXACTLY THE SAME selected spacecraft, not alternate designs. Crisp readable large forms with restrained panel lines. Warm off-white paper background, fine muted blue-gray registration grid, graphite line work, muted ivory ceramic hull, dark petrol canopy, restrained weathered copper leading-edge accents, cyan engine interiors. No space background, no UI, no weapons, no clutter, no separate fins that resemble extra wings.

Fixed single spacecraft design: slender faceted spindle fuselage, tapered pointed nose, broad gently stepped aft shoulder, total length 18 relative units, maximum rear wingspan 15.2, short forward wingspan 11.2. One low elongated smoked teal canopy on upper forward third of fuselage, set back from solid nose tip. Exactly FOUR separate broad trapezoidal wings in two longitudinally separated bilateral pairs: two SHORT forward-swept FORE wings attached near the first third of the body on a slightly raised plane; two LONG aft-swept AFT wings attached near the rear third on a lower plane. Clear open gap between fore and aft wing on EACH side. Fore wings extend forward/outward; aft wings extend backward/outward. Wing tips blunt clipped, no upright fins. The front pair sits HIGHER than the rear pair by 1.4 units, enabling four distinct wing silhouettes in front view. Short fore wings also have a modest upward cant. Rear wings approximately level. There is a continuous central body between all four roots. This is a split tandem four-wing layout, NOT a single X, NOT a four-blade rotor, NOT a biplane with coincident roots. All four must read separately in the top and three-quarter view. Each wing has the same single restrained copper outer leading-edge strip and dark root joint.

Exactly TWO main engine nacelles, elongated dark rectangular/faceted housings mounted beside aft fuselage under rear wing root area, on port and starboard, symmetric. Both point straight backwards and end in ONE circular cyan exhaust each at the tail. No wingtip engines, no front-facing glowing exhaust, no extra thrusters. Engine nacelles flank the hull, not stacked. Compact landing gear retracted, no guns, no tall tail fin.

Sheet composition: 2x2 panels with wide whitespace and thin separating rules. TOP LEFT large true TOP ORTHOGRAPHIC, nose UP, zero perspective, exact left-right symmetry, label "01 TOP"; all FOUR wing panels separated by obvious negative-space slots; canopy in forward third; two nacelles at aft end. TOP RIGHT true FRONT ORTHOGRAPHIC seen from nose, label "02 FRONT"; show the same central canopy, the raised SHORT fore wings above the LONG low aft wings so all FOUR are distinguishable and paired symmetrically. Nacelle front caps beside aft hull may be visible but exhausts do not face viewer. BOTTOM LEFT true PORT SIDE ORTHOGRAPHIC, nose LEFT, label "03 PORT"; show same elongated low canopy, same high short forward wing root and low swept rear wing root, nacelle below aft root; opposite side's wings coincide in orthographic projection, use subtle dashed hidden lines and a small "PORT / STBD OVERLAP" note rather than inventing a fifth wing. BOTTOM RIGHT a large elevated FRONT-PORT three-quarter concept painting, nose toward lower left, label "04 PERSPECTIVE"; view from high enough above to visibly separate all FOUR wings and the longitudinal gaps, showing believable volume and material direction. Exactly the same proportions, canopy, wing root placement, FOUR wing panels and TWO engine nacelles across all panels. Orthographic panels must be precise measured-style concept illustration, perspective panel a tasteful solid industrial design illustration; none are exploded views. Add only small labels "FORE PAIR", "AFT PAIR", "TWIN AFT NACELLES" as useful. Prioritize strict structural correspondence and four-wing readability over detailing or dramatic perspective. No long prose, no extraneous spacecraft variants.

correction.prompt:
Edit this exact AURORA reference sheet to fix structural correspondence. Keep the paper style, TOP, FRONT and PERSPECTIVE spacecraft shapes and materials unchanged; those three panels show the selected design well, including the four independent tandem wings. This is a correction pass of the SAME SHIP, not a new design.

CRITICAL CORRECTION IN LOWER LEFT "03 PORT" ONLY: redraw the wing shapes in the port SIDE orthographic panel so they are a plausible exact side projection of the upper-left TOP design. The nose points LEFT. The SHORT FORWARD-SWEPT fore wing has its outer clipped TIP FORWARD of its dark root: the elevated tip must be to the LEFT of the attachment/root when nose is left. It must NOT slope backwards towards the tail as in the input. The short fore wing is mounted higher; root around the forward-mid fuselage, tip above and slightly forward. The long AFT-SWEPT rear wing has its tip to the RIGHT of its root. Exactly one upper short fore-wing silhouette and one lower long aft-wing silhouette appear in this side projection; the starboard members coincide behind them and must NOT be illustrated as a THIRD independent wing or extra fin. Use a very subtle dashed coincident hidden line plus the existing PORT / STBD OVERLAP note. Remove the little extra blade in the lower-left panel that currently emerges over the nacelle as an additional shorter aft wing. Show only the one long aft wing profile continuing cleanly over/along the one visible engine nacelle. Two rear nacelles overlap in the exact port view; one visible engine is correct. Keep low teal canopy in its same forward third, same pointed nose, faceted central hull, rectangular charcoal nacelle at rear, cyan rear exhaust ONLY at right. Front root plane is above rear root plane. Side diagram should be clean, minimal, legible as a true side view rather than another perspective. No tall tail fin.

Correct dimensional TEXT across the sheet to match the selected illustrated planform: ship length 18.0; rear wingspan 18.6; fore wingspan 12.6. Replace the top-view "11.2" with "12.6" and BOTH "15.2" rear-wingspan labels (TOP and FRONT) with "18.6". Do not change TOP/FRONT/PERSPECTIVE shapes to chase the old dimensions. Leave the small 1.4 root-plane separation as a conceptual target. Add tiny footer "CONCEPT PROPORTIONS / NOT A PRODUCTION DRAWING" if space permits. Keep title AURORA / 01. Preserve the original FOUR-wing count and TWO aft engines everywhere. In the perspective keep both short fore wings and both long rear wings visible, no fifth wing. Crisp high resolution source image, same aspect ratio and panel positions.

side_tail_correction.prompt:
Make ONE local engineering-consistency correction to this same AURORA four-view concept sheet. Preserve TOP, FRONT, and PERSPECTIVE panels exactly, including all four wings, canopy and twin engines; do not redesign anything. Preserve warm cream industrial illustration style.

ONLY the lower-left PORT SIDE drawing is incorrect: its long aft wing projects farther back than the engine nozzle, contradicting the TOP panel, whose wing tips are WELL FORWARD of the twin aft nozzles. Fix that. The nose in this side panel points LEFT, the aft exhaust is to the RIGHT. Shorten and reposition the ONE visible lower AFT WING side profile: its dark root attaches just behind the fuselage midpoint, its swept-back clipped tip ends approximately 83 percent along the overall nose-to-exhaust length, clearly to the LEFT of the rightmost cyan nozzle by about 17 percent of ship length. The aft wing must NOT continue horizontally to the right of the engine or to the dimension endpoint. The engine nozzle, not the wing, is the last rearmost point. Delete the old long rear-wing profile that stretches to the right of the nozzle. Keep the charcoal nacelle below the wing and put its FRONT around 74 percent of the nose-to-nozzle length, its back at the nozzle, so its total length is about a quarter of the ship length; exactly one nacelle is visible because its opposite side overlaps. Show the faceted central hull taper extending to the same aft station as the nozzle, not extending further aft. Adjust the right end of the 18.0 LENGTH arrow to align with the nozzle/hull tail, not the old incorrect wing tip. No extra fins, tabs, blades, or third wings.

Keep the UPPER short FORE WING already forward swept in the port side: its tip is to the LEFT of its dark root, on a higher plane; its root sits roughly 36 to 52 percent of length. Keep the nose shape, elongated single low teal canopy (16 to 43 percent of length), overall shallow body height and fore/aft high-low step. Side view shows one short fore wing and one longer aft wing, with the other side coincident and unobtrusively dashed. Maintain PORT / STBD OVERLAP note. All four views describe the same ship: 18.0 long, 18.6 aft wingspan, 12.6 fore wingspan, one canopy, twin aft nacelles, four separate tandem wings, no tail fin. No perspective in the side drawing; do not add a visible far-side wing. Preserve all other three panels pixel-for-pixel as far as possible.

side_registration.prompt:

Same ship, four tandem wings, no new design. In side panel, nose is x45, aft nozzle x632, so reference length587pixels. Several components are still too far aft relative to TOP view. Use these explicit positions to match TOP view:

1. MOVE the entire raised short FORE WING approximately 85 pixels to the LEFT (forward) from its current position. Its upper clipped forward tip should lie near x235,y770, not x320. Its dark attachment/root along the fuselage should run roughly x260 through x350, around y805. It is a short forward-swept wing mounted near the forward-middle, directly beside/behind the rear half of canopy. Its tip is LEFT of its root. Preserve its copper leading edge. Move the FORE PAIR label leader to the moved wing. This wing must not remain centered around x380.
2. SHORTEN the lower long AFT WING's trailing side projection by approximately 45 pixels at the RIGHT end. Keep its root near x400,y835 but move its clipped aft tip to approximately x540,y830, not x588. That tip is substantially ahead/LEFT of the engine exhaust at x632, consistent with TOP. One low aft wing profile only, no second blade. Its root remains behind the fore root with a clear longitudinal gap.
3. The visible aft ENGINE nacelle should begin near x475, extend to the unchanged cyan nozzle at x632, and stay under the aft-root region. Its front cap is after the forward wing and its back is the rearmost end of the vessel. Shorten the nacelle FRONT rather than moving the nozzle.
4. The one low elongated teal CANOPY begins near x138,y805 and ends near x295,y790; keep it clearly on forward third. Same pointed nose x45, same shallow faceted body, tail taper to x632. Keep the 18.0 dimension line ending at x632.
5. Exactly one near-side fore wing and one near-side aft wing are visible in this true orthographic side view; far-side wings overlap, retain PORT / STBD OVERLAP note. Never add extra fins or wings to compensate. Fore wing remains higher than aft wing. Keep restrained original cream/copper/charcoal colors and fine graphite outlines. Preserve title and all 12.6,18.6,18.0 labels.

This is a precise LOCAL CORRECTION to match the already-correct top planform; DO NOT CHANGE THE TOP, FRONT OR PERSPECTIVE PANELS. High quality same aspect-ratio master sheet.

annotation_correction.prompt:

In lower-left panel "03 PORT", the existing label at the bottom right says "AFT PAIR" but its leader points to the charcoal engine nacelle. Correct ONLY those words to "PORT NACELLE", keeping that leader exactly at the nacelle. The low aft wing is the copper-edged plate immediately above the nacelle; it is already clearly drawn and does not need to be moved or extended. Do not change the "FORE PAIR" label or the PORT / STBD OVERLAP note. Do not change TOP, FRONT or PERSPECTIVE panels. Do not generate a new vessel or add any detail. Highest quality master sheet, same dimensions and aspect ratio. Only the incorrect label becomes PORT NACELLE.
